sentences.text: The accident in the present case took place on 12.07.2017.

It is the case of the petitioner that at around 02:30 PM, he was going to Dharamshila Hospital on his bullet motorcycle registration No.
UP-14-CA-7752.

When he reached near the gate of Dharamshila Hospital, a car (i10) registration No.DL-7CE-9819, driven by its driver respondent no.1 Lalan Mishra in a rash and negligent manner came from the front side and took a turn without giving indicator towards the hospital and hit him.
Due to this accident, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted in Dharamshila Hospital where he remained hospitalised from 12.07.2017 to 18.07.2017.
The injury suffered by him was a fracture of distal phalanx of 3 rd, 4th and 5th fingers (middle, ring and little finger) and fracture of the 3 rd metatarsal proximal aspect.

As per disability certificate, he has suffered 10%
permanent disability in relation to his left upper limb.
3. On notice of the petition, the respondent no. 1 & 2 appeared.

The respondents no. 1 & 2 who are the driver and owner of the offending car have jointly filed their reply and taken the defence that some unknown vehicle caused the accident of the petitioner and fled away from the spot.
The petitioner in collusion with the police in order to secure compensation, falsely implicated them.
4. The respondent no. 3 insurance company - Tata AIG General Insurance Company has taken the general defences.
Further, it is stated that there is discrepancy in the name of victim as Amit Goswami and that he was driving the vehicle without driving licence and his vehicle was not even insured.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 31.01.2018 : -
(i) Whether Mr. Amit Giri sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 12.07.2017 at about 2:50 pm in front of Dharamshila Hospital, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS New Ashok Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL 7CE 9819 (car) by respondent no.1 Lalan Mishra ?

(OPP)
(ii) Whether petitioner was holding a valid driving license to drive the motorcycle bearing No. UP 14 CA 7752 and he contributed to the accident, if so, its extent?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether there was breach of any term and condition of insurance policy ?

OPR3) 
(iv) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?(OPP)
(v) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate of interest and for which period?(OPP)
(vi) Relief 6.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner Amit Giri has examined himself as PW-1.
The respondents have not led any evidence.

sentences.text:
I have heard Mr. Sudhir Goswami, counsel for petitioner and Mr. Ved Vyas Tripathi & Indra Jeet,
counsel for respondent no.3- insurance company and perused the records.

8. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1 : Whether Mr. Amit Giri sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 12.07.2017 at about 2:50 pm in front of Dharamshila Hospital, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS New Ashok Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL 7CE 9819 (car) by respondent no.1 Lalan Mishra ? (OPP)
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
10. Now in this case, the petitioner Amit Giri is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and proved DAR Ex.PW1/1, his aadhar card Ex.PW1/2, driving licence Ex.PW1/3, medical documents Ex.PW1/4 and medical bills Ex.PW1/5.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the car.
He has deposed that on 12.07.2017 at around 02:30 PM, he was going to Dharamshila Hospital on his bullet motorcycle registration No. UP-14-CA-7752.

When he reached near the gate of Dharamshila Hospital, a car (i10) registration No.DL-7CE-9819, driven by its driver respondent no.1 Lalan Mishra in a rash and negligent manner came from the front side and took a turn without giving indicator towards the hospital and hit him.
Due to this accident, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted in Dharamshila Hospital where he remained hospitalised from 12.07.2017 to 18.07.2017.
The injury suffered by him was a fracture of distal phalanx of 3rd, 4th and 5th fingers (middle, ring and little finger).
Fracture of the 3rd metatarsal proximal aspect.
As per disability certificate, he has suffered 10% permanent disability in relation to his left upper limb.

He was working with Nexa as Relationship Manger (Sales and was getting salary of Rs.21,000/- per month.
11.
After investigation, the police filed the chargesheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the car.
Filing of chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima faice points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

sentences.text: 12. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of chargesheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such chargesheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.

In Amit Giri vs Lalan Mishra And Others on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117852190/
3 such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Respondent no.1 the owner/driver of the offending vehicle did not led any evidence to prove any contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.

14. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and for filing of chargesheet, it is proved that the petitioner Amit Giri received injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Lalan Mishra, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No.2 Whether petitioner was holding a valid driving license to drive the motorcycle bearing No. UP 14 CA 7752 and he contributed to the accident, if so, its extent?
The petitioner has proved on record the driving licence Ex.PW1/3.
The burden to prove that his negligence contributed in the accident was upon the respondents.
Respondent did not lead any evidence to show any contributory negligence whereas the petitioner has proved his driving licence.
In view of the same, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No.3.
Whether there was breach of any term and condition of insurance policy ?
(OPR3)
16. The burden to prove this issue was on the respondent no. 3.
But nothing has been put forth or proved that what if any was the breach of any terms and condition of the insurance policy by the respondents.
On record there is a copy of driving licence of the petitioner proved by him as Ex.PW1/3.
There is nothing from the side of insurance company or other respondents against this driving licence.
Therefore, this issue is decided against the respondent no. 3 by holding that there was no breach of any term and condition of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle.
ISSUE No.4 : Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?
OPP 17.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
18. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

Amit Giri vs Lalan Mishra And Others on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117852190/
4 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

entities.text: Amit Giri vs Lalan Mishra And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not resulting loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
Now, in the present case, the injured Amit Giri has suffered a fracture in his upper limb which caused a medical disability of 10%.
Therefore on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows -

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
19.
Petitioner has proved some of his medical bills.
Under this head, actual medical bills are reimbursed.
The bills which are on record are of Rs.68,101/- Therefore, I award Rs.68,101/- as compensation under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
20.
According to his affidavit, after the accident, petitioner remained in hospital for around 6 days that was from 12.07.2017 to 18.07.2017.
But then there is overwriting in the discharge slip and none of the document shows that after 13.07.2017 any treatment was given to him.
In these circumstances, his hospitalzation is considered only of two days.

However, considering that he had crush injuries in his hand and also had a fracture of left foot and also considering the nature of the permanent disability suffered by him which is a clear proof of the amount of pain and suffering, he must have endured in that accident, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.25,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 21.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.5,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and special diet charges.
22. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the Amit Giri vs Lalan Mishra And Others on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117852190/

entities.text: Amit Giri vs Lalan Mishra And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5 petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- as attendant charges.
23. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.10,000/- (5,000+5,000) under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
24.
Petitioner has claimed that he was working as Relationship Manger (Sales) in Nexa and was getting salary of Rs.21,000/- per month.
There is no contrary evidence against this by the respondents.
There is no harm in believing that the petitioner must have been earning this much money as claimed by him.
Therefore, his income is taken as Rs.21,000/- per month.
The evidence of the petitioner shows that he remained hospitalized for around 2 days.
Petitioner in his evidence affidavit stated that he was unable to join his work for 2 months.
Otherwise also it is not difficult to presume that in case of fracture he must have been disabled from work for a least two months as this would have been the minimum time to heel his wound.
Therefore, I award Rs.21,000/-(21,000x2) as compensation under this head.
Therefore, his loss of income for two months is calculated as Rs.42,000/-.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO PERMANENT DISABILITY.
20. The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability.
The disability certificate of Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of 10% disability due fracture in relation to left upper limb.
The doctor has not been examined.
The petitioner has not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.
In his affidavit, he has stated that he was unable to join his work for two months, which means that after two months he would have resumed his job.
Further, he is silent whether he suffered any loss of income after joining the job again.
Therefore, it can be presumed that after unable to join his job for two months, he joined it and started working as before.
Therefore, he has not proved that due to this injury his income has reduced.
But because he has 10% disability due to fracture in left upper limb, it is not difficult to assume that this disability will affect his day-to-day life and profession.
Therefore, I presume that the petitioner must have suffered at least 3% functional disability, also in carrying on with his profession.
In view of this, I believe that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 3% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

On the basis of his income taken as Rs.21,000/- per month, the petitioner's annual income shall be Rs.2,52,000/-.
21.

The copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner shows the date of birth of petitioner was 06.06.1993,
which would mean that he was around 24 years of age at the time of accident and thus, multiplier of 18 would be applicable.

Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 40% has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was under the age of 40 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Amit Giri vs Lalan Mishra And Others on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117852190/
6 Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252, Rajasthan High Court).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The yearly income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs.2,52,000/-.
In this after adding 40% of the future prospects amounting to Rs.1,00,800/-, the yearly income with future prospects will become Rs.3,52,800/-.
In this, yearly income, a multiplier of 16 will make the future income as Rs.3,52,800x18= Rs.63,50,400/-.

3% loss of income due to 3% percent functional disability will mean that the overall loss of income to the petitioner shall be 3% of Rs.63,50,400/-
which will be Rs.1,90,512/-.
Therefore, this amount is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF AMENITIES 22.
Further, the petitioner is granted Rs.10,000/- for loss of amenities.

23. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarised as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1 Medical Expenses Rs.68,101/-
 2 Pain & Sufferings Rs.25,000/-
 3 Conveyance & Special diet Rs.5,000/-
 4 Attendant charges Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of Income during Rs.42,000/-
 treatment  Loss of future income due to Rs.1,90,512/-
 permanent disability
7 Loss
of Amenities

TOTAL Rs.3,45,613/-
Issue No. 3 (iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?
Petitioner has pursued his case diligently.
Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

LIABILITY:
25.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and,
in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.3/ insurance company becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.

Six Hundred & Thirteen only) along with interest @ 6% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3 Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.
